questions.text: A scatter plot shows that students with more practice time tend to score higher. Which conclusion is justified by the plot alone?
answers: Higher scores are proved to cause extra practice
Extra practice is proved to cause every higher score
Practice time and scores are associated; the plot alone does not prove causation
Every student with more practice must score higher
questions.explanation: Observational association alone does not rule out other explanations.

questions.text: Most scatter-plot points cluster near an upward trend, but one point lies far below them. What should an analyst do first?
answers: Check the unusual observation and investigate its context
Delete it automatically so the plot looks cleaner
Change it to the average without checking
Conclude there is no overall pattern
questions.explanation: An outlier may reflect an error or an important real case; investigate before excluding it.
